scene1_screen1.text: Paris always promised passion — but tonight, it delivered temptation at a closed party in masks.

scene1_screen2.text: She entered like a whispered sin in silk. Red satin clung to her body like a second skin. Her mask gleamed — blood-red velvet and mystery. They called her Miss Passion, though she offered no name.

scene1_screen4.text: Across the room, he stood like an unsolved riddle in a tuxedo. A crisp white three-piece suit, a black mask as simple as shadow. They called him Mister Mystery. Eyes like ink. Smile like a dare.

scene1_screen6.text: Their paths crossed at the champagne tower. Fingers brushed — hers chilled, his warm. Neither apologized.

scene1_screen7.text: (lightly, amused) I suppose it’s fitting to meet a stranger over something that bubbles and disappears.

scene1_screen9.text: She didn’t laugh. But her smile deepened. His gaze dipped — collarbone, lips, the soft rise of cleavage framed by satin.

scene1_screen11.text: Only if you want to ruin it.

scene1_screen12.text: A toast, then. Glasses clinked. Her lipstick left a red crescent on the rim — and he watched her tongue catch it.

scene1_screen13.text: Then, a voice rang out above the piano — smooth, mischievous.

scene1_screen14.text: (amplified, playful) Ladies and gentlemen… let’s make tonight even more dangerous. Find someone. Lose the crowd. One hour. One room. No names. No regrets.

scene1_screen15.text: Gasps. Laughter. A ripple of excitement across velvet and lace. Miss Passion turned — slowly. Red silk swaying, her expression unreadable.

scene1_screen18.text: They left the crowd behind — two strangers stitched together by silence and spark. He didn’t touch her hand. He didn’t need to.

scene1_screen19.text: A hallway. A door. 407. Unlocked. Inviting. A threshold between pretending and permission.

scene1_screen20.text: The door clicked shut. He backed her against the wall, deliberate but slow, watching her breath hitch.

scene1_screen21.text: Their masks stayed on. But everything else began to fall.

scene1_screen22.text: His jacket hit the floor. Her gloves slid down her arms. Her breath caught when his lips brushed her neck — not from shock, but from the heat that bloomed between her legs like fire licking silk.

scene1_screen24.text: (low) Only if I get to win.

scene1_screen25.text: She pulled him closer by the tie. Their mouths collided — no buildup, no hesitation. Just hunger. The kind that couldn’t wait for morning. The kind that never asked for names.

scene1_screen26.text: He lifted her onto the bed without breaking the kiss. Her legs wrapped around his waist as if they already knew the rhythm.

scene1_screen27.text: She gasped when his hands found bare skin beneath red fabric — her back arching to meet his touch.

scene1_screen28.text: The room blurred. The city outside ceased to exist. There was only sweat. Only breath. Only them.

scene1_screen29.text: Clothes came off. He explored her like someone rediscovering a long-lost secret. She pressed her nails into his shoulders like punctuation — marking the places where he made her lose herself.

scene1_screen30.text: On top. Then beneath. Then tangled limbs and sheets and sighs and silence.

scene1_screen31.text: His lips found her throat. Her mouth found his name — but didn’t say it. It hovered there, unspoken. Like a secret too sacred to ruin.

scene1_screen32.text: Time warped. Hours melted. Sleep crept in like a quiet thief.

scene1_screen33.text: She rested her head on his chest, listening to the steady beat of a heart she would never touch again. At least — that was the plan.

scene1_screen34.text: Morning after, he stirred and reached for her. The bed was still warm, but empty. On the pillow: her red mask. A glass of water on the nightstand. No note. No scent.

scene1_screen35.text: Just the lingering trace of her skin on his fingertips. And the ache of a man who’d had something real — and let it vanish with the dawn.

scene1_screen36.text: He laid back down. Eyes open. Wondering if she had been real at all. Or just a fever dream of silk and sin.

scene2_screen1.text: Janice walks in like she owns the air around her. Tailored blazer, neutral lipstick, heels low, but sharp. Every step says: I belong here. Every nerve says: Ignore last Saturday.

scene2_screen2.text: She takes her seat, places her notepad down. Smooth. Saturday night is folded away. Red silk tucked in a drawer. This is real life: spreadsheets and elevations.

scene2_screen4.text: At the head of the table. One arm slung over blueprint folders. The other near his mouth, hiding what is definitely a smirk. Their eyes lock. One second. Maybe two.

scene2_screen6.text: (turning to the room) Good morning, everyone. I’m Janice Wright, project coordinator for Montreuil. Happy to be on board.

scene2_screen7.text: A few polite nods. A smile from the intern. But across the table, the real welcome? It’s Henry’s eyes — still fixed on her like she’s the blueprint that doesn’t follow regulations.

scene2_screen8.text: (dry) Henry Clarke. Consultant from the board. Here to optimize foundations, mitigate risks, and maybe fix the coffee machine.

scene2_screen9.text: A chuckle here. A throat clear there. But between them? Nothing moves, nothing breathes.

scene2_screen10.text: The meeting continues — slide decks, cost projections, permit chatter. Janice scribbles notes with crisp efficiency. Henry answers questions with dry wit and undeniable authority.

scene2_screen11.text: They don’t look at each other. But they don’t need to.

scene2_screen12.text: She feels the weight of his attention every time she speaks. He notes the curve of her mouth when she corrects a vendor mistake.

scene2_screen13.text: By the time the meeting ends, the air is warm with what no one will name. Colleagues file out — a few linger near the door, eyeing them subtly.

scene2_screen14.text: (casually) Janice — you’re visiting the Montreuil site today, right?

scene2_screen16.text: (already standing) Perfect. Our driver’s waiting outside.

scene2_screen17.text: One of the junior architects glances between them. Just a flicker full of curiosity.

scene2_screen18.text: Janice gathers her things. Nothing in her movement suggests she remembers the sound of his voice in the dark. But everything in his smile says he hasn’t forgotten a thing.

scene2_screen19.text: They stand side by side. Waiting for the car. Not touching. Not speaking. But the tension? As thick as steam over strong espresso.

scene2_screen20.text: His gaze flicks toward her. She doesn’t look — but she knows. He’s remembering, and so is she.

scene2_choice1.text: How do you handle the wait?

opts.text: Keep it light. But let her know you remember.
Lean in, enough to taste the tension.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen1.text: (light) So... do you always vanish before sunrise, or was I just lucky?

scene2_choice1_option1_screen2.text: (side-eye, dry) You snored. I took it as my cue.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen4.text: Shame. I had plans: croissants, bad coffee, morning silence... and maybe round two.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen7.text: The street noise fades. Just two voices. And everything they’re not saying.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen1.text: (half-smile) I didn’t expect to see you again. At least... not dressed.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (archly) The office doesn’t allow red satin and stilettos.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen3.text: A pity. You wore them well.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen4.text: A pause. Too short to matter, too long to ignore.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (quiet) You wore a mask. But you didn’t hide.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen4.text: His eyes drop — her lips, her collarbone, the edge of her blouse.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen5.text: (voice rough) Tell me to back off. And I will.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen7.text: The moment lands between them — heavy, quiet. But neither moves. Not for another heartbeat.

scene2_screen21.text: The black car glides to a stop. The window rolls down.

scene2_screen24.text: He opens the door. She slides in — legs crossed, posture perfect. But her breath? A little faster than before.

scene2_screen25.text: He follows. Sits closer than he should. Their knees brush. Not accidental, not apologetic, just deliberate. No masks now. But the game? Still very much in play.

scene3_screen1.text: The car door clicks shut behind them. And with it — everything else. Just leather seats, rainfall, and a silence that hums with memory.

scene3_screen2.text: Henry taps a button. The divider slides up, severing them from the driver. Not a wall, but a boundary, a permission.

scene3_screen3.text: (offhand, too casual) Just in case the traffic gets... intimate.

scene3_screen4.text: Janice doesn’t flinch. Doesn’t even glance his way. She crosses her legs — deliberate, smooth. A whisper of fabric. The faintest shift in perfume.

scene3_screen5.text: He notices. Of course he does.

scene3_screen6.text: (light, teasing) You’re very composed… for someone who once told me to bite more quietly.

scene3_screen7.text: (still facing forward) You’re very smug… for someone who actually did it

scene3_screen8.text: His laugh is low. Dark chocolate and heat. It rolls through the space between them like a question she’s not ready to answer.

scene3_screen9.text: I’ve been wondering. Which one of us is faking it harder?

scene3_screen10.text: She slowly turns, eyes like glass over flame.

scene3_screen11.text: I’m not faking. That night was real. And it ended.

scene3_screen13.text: The question lands in her lap, heavy and true. The kind you don’t answer unless you’re ready for everything to change.

scene3_screen14.text: Outside, Paris slips by in greys and golds. Inside, the space between them crackles.

scene3_screen15.text: (softly) You left before I could ask your name. Now I know it. But I don’t know you.

scene3_screen16.text: (dry) That was the point of the mask, wasn’t it?

scene3_screen17.text: He shifts slightly. Not closer — but not away.  His hand trails along the seam of the seat, near, but not touching.

scene3_screen18.text: (low, sincere) Tell me something honest. Right now.

scene3_screen19.text: Why would I want to do that?

scene3_screen20.text: (voice like velvet and danger) Because if you don’t, then I will. And I promise you, you’ll be the one distracted in Montreuil.

opts.text: Give in, let the tension win.
Play with fire, but don’t touch it.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen1.text: She turns fully. One leg brushes his.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen3.text: She leans in — slow, controlled — until her mouth is a breath from his jaw.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen4.text: (whisper) I’ve been thinking about your mouth since Saturday.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen6.text: (gravel) I’ve been thinking about how you sounded when you begged me not to stop.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen7.text: They move at once. His hand finds the back of her neck. Her mouth crashes into his. The kiss is fire. Unapologetic. Unrelenting.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen8.text: She climbs into his lap like memory is muscle. He drags her closer like he needs her to breathe.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen9.text: Her blouse parts beneath his fingers. His belt buckle clinks. But they don’t go further. They don’t need to. Not yet.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen10.text: Windows fog. The car shifts slightly. The driver’s voice breaks through.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen12.text: She pulls back. Breathless. Smooths her hair. Rebuttons her shirt.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen13.text: (smiling as she opens the door) Don’t forget to pick me up later. We’re far from done.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen1.text: She tilts her head — a slow, dangerous arc.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen3.text: She leans in — not to kiss, but close enough for her words to graze his ear.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen4.text: (whisper) I still remember how you taste.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen6.text: (pulling back, teasing) And I’m very good at self-control. Are you?

scene3_choice1_option2_screen9.text: The car slows. She steps out. Calm. Clean lines, immaculate composure. He stays behind, staring, still tasting her words.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen2.text: She turns away. Legs crossed the other way now. Distance reasserted.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen3.text: It was one night. Beautiful, irrepeatable. And irrelevant now.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen4.text: He watches her. Expression unreadable — except for the tension in his jaw.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen5.text: Let’s not break something that didn’t promise to last.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen8.text: She leaves. And for the first time in years, he’s not sure how to follow.

scene3_screen21.text: Later — they ride together again. Same seats. Same silence. But now it’s changed: not absence, not discomfort. Just the weight of what’s already been said — or tasted — or left unsaid.

scene3_screen22.text: Because the moment passed, but nothing about them is finished.

scene4_screen1.text: The road home winds through the sleepy hush of Paris. They ride in silence, not out of discomfort — but because neither wants to break whatever this is.

scene4_screen3.text: Janice looks up, blinks once, then turns to Henry with a skeptical brow.

scene4_screen5.text: (confused) No, miss. This is the address Mr. Clarke provided.

scene4_screen10.text: Penthouse left. Corner view. The bakery. Let me guess — lemon tree?

scene4_screen11.text: (groaning) Penthouse right. It’s my lemon tree.

scene4_screen12.text: Been mocking me every morning I wake up late.

scene4_screen13.text: They stare at each other. Then — laughter. Real. Unscripted. The kind that softens everything.

scene4_screen14.text: (still smiling) Of all the buildings in Paris..

scene4_screen16.text: She looks at him — not the colleague, not the stranger from the masquerade — but the man who somehow keeps showing up exactly where she is.

scene4_screen17.text: (quieter now) Do you believe in... timing?

scene4_screen18.text: (honest, not teasing) Lately, I believe in coincidence with a grudge. Like the universe is trying to make a point.

scene4_screen19.text: Janice doesn’t reply — not with words. But something in her posture shifts. Open, for just a moment. Vulnerable, but not weak.

scene4_screen20.text: They step into the grand lobby. Their footsteps echo lightly against marble. The quiet isn't empty — it's weighted.

scene4_screen21.text: At the elevator, they stand close. Too close to pretend it’s still professional. Not touching — but no longer avoiding it either.

scene4_screen22.text: Henry’s hand brushes hers. Not by accident. Not anymore.

scene4_screen23.text: (soft) You ever get the feeling something’s already decided — but still asking permission?

scene4_screen24.text: Janice turns to him slowly. Eyes dark, unreadable — but not closed.

scene4_screen25.text: Maybe. Or maybe we just keep ending up in the same story.

scene4_screen26.text: A bell chimes. The elevator doors slide open. They step outside. Together.

scene4_choice1.text: How do you handle this… coincidence?

opts.text: Say goodbye and leave everything as is.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen1.text: They pause at their doors. Keys halfway turned.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen2.text: (mild) You want to keep pretending we’re just neighbors? Or are we at least admitting it’s a little weird now?

scene4_choice1_option1_screen4.text: Then maybe one glass to toast our absurd luck? Neighbors don’t need to be strangers.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen5.text: She considers. Then nods, just once.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen6.text: Inside her place: a bottle of wine. Two mismatched glasses. Conversation that loosens shoulders.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen7.text: (teasing) If you say one more thing about fate, I’m kicking you out.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen8.text: Not fate. Just… geography. With benefits.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen9.text: The vibe stays light. Friendly. A little charged — but both hold the line. Eventually, he leaves with a smirk and a “Goodnight, neighbor.”

scene4_choice1_option1_screen10.text: She watches the door a beat too long before locking it.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen11.text: Morning. Sunlight streaming over the phone on a bed shelf featuring one message from him. No emojis. Just: “See you around. Or across the hall.”

scene4_choice1_option2_screen1.text: They stop at her door. A quiet tension settling in.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (soft) So what happens if we stop pretending?

scene4_choice1_option2_screen3.text: (low, honest) Then we stop lying to ourselves.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen4.text: She opens the door. He follows. The city glows behind the glass, but neither looks outside.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen5.text: Wine is poured but never touched. He touches her shoulder — and that’s it. Her breath catches. Then lips. Hands. Her blouse. His jacket. No time to reach the bed.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen6.text: They crash to the couch in a mess of laughter and heat. He lifts her like she weighs nothing. She pulls him in like she hasn’t stopped wanting him.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen7.text: They undress each other slowly — not rushed, but with urgency born of memory.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen8.text: The city forgets them. The night forgives them. Nothing polite. Nothing held back.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen9.text: She wakes alone. A note rests on the nightstand. “Didn’t want to ruin your morning. Don’t be late to work. — H.”

scene4_choice1_option2_screen10.text: She smiles into the pillow. Paris, apparently, has excellent timing.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen1.text: They reach their doors in silence. No jokes. No sparks.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (formal) Well. Looks like we’re neighbors. Small world.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen7.text: The doors close. Together, but not connected. Behind them: two apartments. Two people wide awake. One what-if.

scene5_screen1.text: Janice hasn’t seen him all day. Just a nod. A glance in passing. Exactly what she claimed she wanted.

scene5_screen2.text: But now it’s after 8 p.m. The office hum has faded. The only sound is the buzz of fluorescent lights — and her thoughts.

scene5_screen3.text: She adjusts an element on her design. Deletes it. Tries again. Focus slips like silk from her fingers.

scene5_screen4.text: She sighs. Rubs the bridge of her nose. Then — the door creaks open behind her.

scene5_screen5.text: (without turning) You forgot how to knock?

scene5_screen6.text: (low, amused) You forgot how to lock it.

scene5_screen7.text: She looks up. He’s there — in the doorway. Casual, yes. But never just that.

scene5_screen8.text: Rolled-up sleeves. Slightly unruly hair. That infuriating calm that only ever spells danger.

scene5_screen11.text: (walking in) And strangely devoid of eye contact.

scene5_screen12.text: (dry) Maybe I was trying something new. Emotional hygiene.

scene5_screen13.text: He closes the door behind him — with a click that feels louder than it should.

scene5_screen14.text: (quieter now) You’ve been biting your lip every time I walk by.

scene5_screen18.text: He steps around the desk. Not hurried — deliberate. She smells his cologne before she sees his shadow on the table.

scene5_screen19.text: (soft) You think this is a mistake.

scene5_screen20.text: (measured) I think it’s reckless. Unprofessional. Complicated.

scene5_screen22.text: She stands. Slowly. They’re eye to eye now. Heat to heat. Every nerve in her body is braced — not against him, but against herself.

scene5_screen24.text: (gentle correction) Independent contractor. Different division. No power dynamics.

scene5_screen26.text: (quiet) I’m not here to be safe, Janice. I’m here because you’re in my head. And under my skin.

scene5_choice1.text: How will the evening continue at the office?

opts.text: Kiss him hard, shut out everything else.
Slow things down, talk, but don’t push him away.
Shut it down, set boundaries for both of you.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen1.text: She doesn’t answer. Just grabs his tie.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen2.text: Their mouths collide — not cautious, not curious. Consuming.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen3.text: He lifts her onto the desk. Papers scatter to the floor. Her legs wrap around him like she never means to let go.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen4.text: His hands slip under her blazer. Her breath catches against his neck. She rocks her hips — chasing heat, and finding fire.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen5.text: Their kiss turns ragged. Their movements get rough, familiar, full of need. It’s not about romance. It’s about everything they’ve tried not to feel, all at once.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen6.text: Later — the office is quiet again. She sits on the edge of her desk. Shirt half-buttoned. Lipstick smudged. Alone.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen7.text: He’s gone — no apology, no regret. So typical.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen8.text: She opens her laptop. Checks her email.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen9.text: “Janice Wright and Henry Clarke have been selected for the Le Blanc Château client site review. Departure: Friday morning. Two nights. Private driver arranged.”

scene5_choice1_option1_screen10.text: She stares. Then exhales a laugh — dry, startled, almost bitter.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen1.text: She puts a hand on his chest. Not rejection — just resistance.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (quiet) I want this. But not tonight. Not in an empty office.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen3.text: He meets her gaze. Steady. Patient.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen4.text: (soft) So we don’t rush. Just tell me you’re not walking away.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen6.text: He leans in. Presses his forehead to hers.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen8.text: Later, she sits alone. Still in her work clothes, mug of tea cooling beside her. The quiet feels softer now.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen10.text: “Janice Wright and Henry Clarke have been selected for the Le Blanc Château client site review. Departure: Friday morning. Two nights. Private driver arranged.”

scene5_choice1_option3_screen1.text: She steps back. Crosses her arms.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (firm) This can’t happen again. It was one night. It has to stay that way.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen3.text: He doesn’t argue. Just studies her for a long moment.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen5.text: He turns. Walks to the door. Leaves without another word.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen7.text: Not because she has more work. Because standing still feels like the only way to keep from falling.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen9.text: “Janice Wright and Henry Clarke have been selected for the Le Blanc Château client site review. Departure: Friday morning. Two nights. Private driver arranged.”

scene5_choice1_option3_screen10.text: She leans back. Covers her eyes with one hand.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen11.text: (wry, to the ceiling) Timing, you petty bastard.

scene5_screen27.text: Some stories end in boardrooms. Others? In quiet rooms with too much tension and not enough distance.

scene5_screen28.text: This one? It’s just getting interesting.

scene6_screen1.text: Le Blanc Château, evening. A private countryside estate outside Paris. Ivy climbs the stone walls. Soft firelight glows behind tall windows.

scene6_screen2.text: By day, they’d been perfect. Colleagues. Professionals. Silent glances beneath polished conversation.

scene6_screen3.text: But the work is over. The rooms are quiet. And the masks — waiting.

scene6_screen4.text: Janice steps inside. Her hair is down. A simple dress hugs her curves. She sees the masks — and her breath hitches.

scene6_screen6.text: (from the shadows) I never left them.

scene6_screen7.text: He steps forward. In one hand — his black mask. In the other — a small, gift-wrapped box.

scene6_screen8.text: (gently) This wasn’t just a business trip. I asked for it. Because I wanted time. With you. No office. No schedules. Just… us.

scene6_screen9.text: She blinks — stunned, breath caught between disbelief and something far more dangerous. But he doesn’t hesitate. He places the small box in her hands, his voice low, certain.

scene6_screen10.text: This isn’t just a memory. It’s yours now. Whatever you choose… I’ll follow.

scene6_screen11.text: Her fingers tremble as she lifts the lid. Inside — his mask. The same one that once promised no names, no consequences. Now, it promises the opposite.

scene6_screen12.text: She looks up — at him. At the man behind the charm and teasing. No words. Just eyes full of fire, ache, and something unspoken — something that dares him to leap.

scene6_screen13.text: She doesn’t answer. She doesn’t have to. Because in that moment, everything in her gaze tells him: If you’re brave enough — the rest is ours.

scene6_choice1.text: What do you offer her tonight?

opts.text: Offer her everything — your love, your body, your future.
Let go. For real. With gratitude.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen1.text: He steps closer. Cups her cheek. His voice low, raw.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen2.text: I don’t want another night. I want all of them. The wild, the quiet, the complicated. Let’s stop pretending.  Be mine — fully.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen3.text: She doesn't answer. She simply kisses him.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen4.text: Not like the first time — desperate and daring. This one is slow, it’s sensual, it’s certain.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen5.text: Clothes fall, but this time — they savor. He lays her down on the bed like she’s something he’s afraid to lose. Their mouths explore, their hands map familiar territory with reverence.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen6.text: Every sigh, every arch of her body, every gasp — says yes. To him. To this. To what’s next.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen7.text: Later, as they lie tangled in sheets and each other, he traces her spine and speaks — soft but sure.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen8.text: I'm leaving the project. No more board. No more contract. Nothing between us but choice.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen9.text: She stares at him. Heart loud. Breath caught.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen1.text: He holds out the mask — but doesn’t push.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen2.text: We’re incredible together. But if now’s not the time… Let’s not ruin it trying to force more. Be my friend. And if more ever feels right — I’ll still be here.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen3.text: She takes the mask. Smiles gently.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen4.text: You might be the only man who makes friendship sound like a love letter.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen6.text: They sit together on the bed. Talking. Laughing. And though the masks remain untouched… The hope in the room is louder than silence.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen1.text: He sets the masks down. Steps back.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen2.text: Maybe this was lightning. One night. A story we get to keep. But I’m tired of chasing a future that keeps slipping away.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen3.text: Her throat tightens. But she nods.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen6.text: They walk together to the balcony. Look out at the French countryside. Then part with a kiss — soft and final.

scene7_screen1.text: In the months that follow, they work. They travel. They live.

scene7_screen2.text: One rainy evening, a note on her kitchen counter. Unfolded carefully, handwritten. “Next time, it’s your turn to bring the masks. Dinner’s in Rome. — H.”

scene7_screen3.text: She smiles. Because whatever comes next — it’s not pretend. It’s just beginning.

scene7_screen4.text: Some nights are meant to end. Others… are meant to begin something else. Would you sneak away from a masquerade… or stay till sunrise? Talk it over in chat — no masks this time. 💬🎭
